case_name: State of Kerala v A. Pareed Pillai and Another
respondent:
A. Pareed Pillai and Another
Supreme Court of India

28 April 1972
Cr.A. No. 71 of 1969 (Arising as an appeal from the Judgment and Order, Dt. 20 August 1968 of the Kerala High Court in Cr.A. No. 174 of 1967).
The Judgment was delivered by: KHANNA, J.
1.  The Three brothers Pareed Pillai, Kader Pillai and Mohammed Pillai, partners of A. Pareed Pillai and Bros., Alwaye as well as K.M. Kurian, Assistant Goods Clerk in the Southern Railway at Alwaye were tried in the court of Special Judge, Trichur for an offence under Section 120-B, Indian Penal Code on the following charge :
"That you (1) Shri A. Pareed Pillai, (2) Sri A. Kader Pillai (3) Sri A. Mohammed Pillai and (4) Sri K. M. Kurian, accused 1 to 4 between December 1962 or earlier and June 1963, at Alwaye agreed to do an illegal act or acts, to wit, accused Nos. 1 and 2 to present forwarding notes in respect of coconut oil tins to be booked without actually tendering tins with coconut oil, but only some empty tins
facts: The Three brothers Pareed Pillai, Kader Pillai and Mohammed Pillai, partners of A. Pareed Pillai and Bros., Alwaye as well as K.M. Kurian, Assistant Goods Clerk in the Southern Railway at Alwaye were tried in the court of Special Judge, Trichur for an offence under Section 120-B, Indian Penal Code on the following charge :
The prosecution case is that the business of firm A. Pareed Pillai and Bros. was to sell coconut oil and to send it by rail to different places in India.
It had been engaged in this business for over 15 years.
As a result of dealing in forward contracts, the firm suffered losses in the end of 1962 and the beginning of 1963.
issues: What is the nature of the conspiracy alleged?
Is the evidence sufficient to prove the offence of cheating?
Can the accused be convicted for the offence under Section 120-B, Indian Penal Code?
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution case is that the business of firm A. Pareed Pillai and Bros. was to sell coconut oil and to send it by rail to different places in India.
As a result of dealing in forward contracts, the firm suffered losses in the end of 1962 and the beginning of 1963.
respondent_arguments: The plea of Pareed and Kader accused was that the demand drafts used to be sent to the bank.
court_reasoning: The court held that the prosecution had established a prima facie case against the accused.
The court also held that the evidence was sufficient to prove the offence of cheating.
holding: Appeal No. 71 of 1969 was filed by the State of Kerala against the acquittal of Pareed and Kader accused.
The conviction of Kurian accused was maintained only for the offence u/s. 5(2), read with S. 5(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.
